problem_description.description: Arkady wants to have a dinner. He has just returned from a shop where he has bought a semifinished cutlet. He only needs to fry it. The cutlet should be fried for 2n seconds, in particular, it should be fried for n seconds on one side and n seconds on the other side. Arkady has already got a frying pan and turn on fire, but understood that maybe he won't be able to flip the cutlet exactly after n seconds after the beginning of cooking.Arkady is too busy with sorting sticker packs in his favorite messenger and can flip the cutlet only in some periods of time. Namely, there are k periods of time in which he can do it, the i-th of them is an interval of time from li seconds after he starts cooking till ri seconds, inclusive. Arkady decided that it's not required to flip the cutlet exactly in the middle of cooking, instead, he will flip it several times in such a way that the cutlet will be fried exactly n seconds on one side and n seconds on the other side in total.Help Arkady and find out if it's possible for him to cook the cutlet, if he is able to flip the cutlet only in given periods of time; and if yes, find the minimum number of flips he needs to cook the cutlet.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000, 1 ≤ k ≤ 100) — the number of seconds the cutlet should be cooked on each side and number of periods of time in which Arkady can flip it. The next k lines contain descriptions of these intervals. Each line contains two integers li and ri (0 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ 2·n), meaning that Arkady can flip the cutlet in any moment starting from li seconds after the beginning of cooking and finishing at ri seconds after beginning of cooking. In particular, if li = ri then Arkady can flip the cutlet only in the moment li = ri. It's guaranteed that li > ri - 1 for all 2 ≤ i ≤ k.
problem_description.output_spec: Output "Hungry" if Arkady won't be able to fry the cutlet for exactly n seconds on one side and exactly n seconds on the other side. Otherwise, output "Full" in the first line, and the minimum number of times he should flip the cutlet in the second line.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first example Arkady should flip the cutlet in time moment 3 seconds after he starts cooking and in time moment 13 seconds after he starts cooking.In the second example, Arkady can flip the cutlet at 10 seconds after he starts cooking.

import sys

class FastScanner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.buffer = bytearray(0x10000)
        self.buffer_offset = 0
        self.buffer_length = 0
        self.is_end_of_file = False
        self.stdin = sys.stdin.buffer

    def read(self):
        data = self.stdin.read(0x10000)
        if data:
            self.buffer = data
            self.buffer_length = len(data)
            self.buffer_offset = 0
        else:
            self.buffer_length = 0
            self.is_end_of_file = True

    def next_byte(self):
        if self.buffer_offset == self.buffer_length:
            if not self.is_end_of_file:
                self.read()
            if self.is_end_of_file:
                return 0
        byte_val = self.buffer[self.buffer_offset]
        self.buffer_offset += 1
        return byte_val

    def next_int(self):
        a = 0
        is_negative = False

        b = self.next_byte()
        while b <= ord(' '):
            b = self.next_byte()
        if b == ord('-'):
            is_negative = True
            b = self.next_byte()
        while b > ord(' '):
            a = a * 10 + (b - ord('0'))
            b = self.next_byte()
        return -a if is_negative else a


kbeg = []
kend = []
n = 0
k = 0
numRotates = 0
minNumRotates = 0


def SaveRotates(num):
    global minNumRotates
    if minNumRotates == 0:
        minNumRotates = num
    else:
        minNumRotates = min(minNumRotates, num)


def CalcRotates(side, tmin, tmax, noffset, koffset, isInterval):
    global numRotates, minNumRotates, kbeg, kend, n, k

    if tmin[0] > n or tmin[1] > n:
        return
    elif ((tmin[0] <= n and tmax[0] >= n) or (tmin[1] <= n and tmax[1] >= n)):
        if ((tmax[0] < n and side == 1) or (tmax[1] < n and side == 0)):
            SaveRotates(numRotates + 1)
        else:
            SaveRotates(numRotates)
        return
    elif koffset == k:
        return

    if isInterval:
        if kbeg[koffset] == kend[koffset]:
            # no rotate
            CalcRotates(side, tmin, tmax, noffset, koffset + 1, False)

            # rotate
            numRotates += 1
            CalcRotates(1 - side, tmin, tmax, noffset, koffset + 1, False)
            numRotates -= 1

        else:
            # no rotate
            tmin[side] += kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            tmax[side] += kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            CalcRotates(side, tmin, tmax, kend[koffset], koffset + 1, False)
            tmin[side] -= kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            tmax[side] -= kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]

            # rotate once
            tmax[side] += kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            tmax[1 - side] += kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            numRotates += 1
            CalcRotates(1 - side, tmin, tmax, kend[koffset], koffset + 1, False)
            numRotates -= 1
            tmax[side] -= kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            tmax[1 - side] -= kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]

            # rotate twice
            tmax[side] += kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            tmin[1 - side] += 1
            tmax[1 - side] += kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset] - 1
            numRotates += 2
            CalcRotates(side, tmin, tmax, kend[koffset], koffset + 1, False)
            numRotates -= 2
            tmax[side] -= kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset]
            tmin[1 - side] -= 1
            tmax[1 - side] -= kend[koffset] - kbeg[koffset] - 1

    else:
        tmin[side] += kbeg[koffset] - noffset
        tmax[side] += kbeg[koffset] - noffset
        CalcRotates(side, tmin, tmax, kbeg[koffset], koffset, True)
        tmin[side] -= kbeg[koffset] - noffset
        tmax[side] -= kbeg[koffset] - noffset


def main():
    global kbeg, kend, n, k, numRotates, minNumRotates

    scanner = FastScanner()
    n = scanner.next_int()
    k = scanner.next_int()

    kbeg = [0] * k
    kend = [0] * k

    for i in range(k):
        kbeg[i] = scanner.next_int()
        kend[i] = scanner.next_int()

    tmin = [0, 0]
    tmax = [0, 0]

import sys
import array
from collections import deque

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data:
        return
    it = iter(data)
    
    n = int(next(it))
    K = int(next(it))
    
    ts = []
    all_len = 0
    for _ in range(K):
        a = int(next(it))
        b = int(next(it))
        ts.append((a, b))
        all_len += b - a
    
    INF = 99999999
    dpe = [INF] * (n + 1)
    dpo = [INF] * (n + 1)
    
    if ts[0][0] > n:
        print("Hungry")
        return
    
    dpe[ts[0][0]] = 0
    
    for i in range(K):
        ndpo = [INF] * (n + 1)
        ndpe = [INF] * (n + 1)
        
        w = ts[i][1] - ts[i][0]
        dq = deque()
        
        # First pass: from dpe to ndpo and ndpe
        for j in range(n + 1):
            while dq and dpe[dq[-1]] >= dpe[j]:
                dq.pop()
            while dq and dq[0] < j - w:
                dq.popleft()
            dq.append(j)
            ndpo[j] = min(ndpo[j], dpe[dq[0]] + 1)
            if j + w <= n:
                ndpe[j + w] = min(ndpe[j + w], dpe[j])
        
        dq.clear()
        
        # Second pass: from dpo to ndpe and ndpo
        for j in range(n + 1):
            while dq and dpo[dq[-1]] >= dpo[j]:
                dq.pop()
            while dq and dq[0] < j - w:
                dq.popleft()
            dq.append(j)
            ndpe[j] = min(ndpe[j], dpo[dq[0]] + 1)
            ndpo[j] = min(ndpo[j], dpo[j])
        
        dpo = ndpo
        dpe = ndpe
        
        # Update dpe and dpo with one-step transitions
        for j in range(n + 1):
            dpe[j] = min(dpe[j], dpo[j] + 1)
            dpo[j] = min(dpo[j], dpe[j] + 1)
        
        # Shift for next interval
        s = (2 * n if i == K - 1 else ts[i + 1][0]) - ts[i][1]
        for j in range(n, s - 1, -1):
            dpe[j] = dpe[j - s]
        for j in range(min(n, s - 1), -1, -1):
            dpe[j] = INF
    
    ans = min(dpe[n], dpo[n])
    if ans >= INF:
        print("Hungry")
    else:
        print("Full")
        print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

            self.buffer = b''
            self.pos = 0
            self.size = 0

        def getc(self):
            if self.pos >= self.size:
                self.buffer = self.in_stream.read(1 << 15)
                self.size = len(self.buffer)
                self.pos = 0
                if self.size == 0:
                    return -1
            ch = self.buffer[self.pos]
            self.pos += 1
            return ch

            while c <= 32:

                if c == -1:
                    return -1
            a = 0
            while c > 32:

                c = self.getc()

        self.cost = [0] * self.m_
        self.cc = [0] * (self.m_ * 2)
        self.m_ = 0

        self.m_ += 1
        self.uu[h] = u
        self.vv[h] = v
        self.uv[h] = u ^ v
        self.cost[h] = cos
        self.cc[h << 1] = cap
        self.aa_[u].append(h << 1)
        self.aa_[v].append(h << 1 | 1)

    def enqueue(self, v):
        if self.iq[v]:
            return
        if self.head + self.cnt == self.nq:
            if self.cnt * 2 <= self.nq:
                self.qq[0:self.cnt] = self.qq[self.head:self.head + self.cnt]
            else:
                self.nq *= 2
                qq_ = [0] * self.nq
                qq_[0:self.cnt] = self.qq[self.head:self.head + self.cnt]
                self.qq = qq_
            self.head = 0
        self.qq[self.head + self.cnt] = v
        self.cnt += 1
        self.iq[v] = True

    def dequeue(self):
        u = self.qq[self.head]
        self.head += 1
        self.cnt -= 1
        self.iq[u] = False
        return u

    def spfa(self, s, t):

        self.pi[s] = 0
        self.head = 0
        self.cnt = 0
        self.enqueue(s)
        while self.cnt > 0:

            adj = self.aa_[u]
            for h_ in adj:

                    p = self.pi[u] + (self.cost[h] if (h_ & 1) == 0 else -self.cost[h])

                    if self.pi[v] > p or (self.pi[v] == p and self.dd[v] > d):
                        self.pi[v] = p
                        self.dd[v] = d
                        self.bb[v] = h_
                        self.enqueue(v)

    def push(self, s, t):
        c = self.INF
        u = t
        while u != s:
            h_ = self.bb[u]
            h = h_ >> 1
            c = min(c, self.cc[h_])
            u ^= self.uv[h]
        u = t
        while u != s:
            h_ = self.bb[u]
            h = h_ >> 1
            self.cc[h_] -= c
            self.cc[h_ ^ 1] += c
            u ^= self.uv[h]

    def push1(self, s, t):
        u = t
        while u != s:
            h_ = self.bb[u]
            h = h_ >> 1
            self.cc[h_] -= 1
            self.cc[h_ ^ 1] += 1
            u ^= self.uv[h]

    def edmonds_karp(self, s, t):
        while self.spfa(s, t):
            self.push1(s, t)
        c = 0
        for h in range(self.m_):
            c += self.cost[h] * self.cc[h << 1 | 1]
        return c

        for i in range(n):

                v = u + 1
                self.link(u, v, k, 0 if i == 0 else c)
        for h in range(k):

        self.println(self.edmonds_karp(self.n_ - 1, 0 * t + t - 1))

problem_description.description: Getting closer and closer to a mathematician, Serval becomes a university student on math major in Japari University. On the Calculus class, his teacher taught him how to calculate the expected length of a random subsegment of a given segment. Then he left a bonus problem as homework, with the award of a garage kit from IOI. The bonus is to extend this problem to the general case as follows.You are given a segment with length $$$l$$$. We randomly choose $$$n$$$ segments by choosing two points (maybe with non-integer coordinates) from the given segment equiprobably and the interval between the two points forms a segment. You are given the number of random segments $$$n$$$, and another integer $$$k$$$. The $$$2n$$$ endpoints of the chosen segments split the segment into $$$(2n+1)$$$ intervals. Your task is to calculate the expected total length of those intervals that are covered by at least $$$k$$$ segments of the $$$n$$$ random segments.You should find the answer modulo $$$998244353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: First line contains three space-separated positive integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ and $$$l$$$ ($$$1\leq k \leq n \leq 2000$$$, $$$1\leq l\leq 10^9$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer — the expected total length of all the intervals covered by at least $$$k$$$ segments of the $$$n$$$ random segments modulo $$$998244353$$$. Formally, let $$$M = 998244353$$$. It can be shown that the answer can be expressed as an irreducible fraction $$$\frac{p}{q}$$$, where $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ are integers and $$$q \not \equiv 0 \pmod{M}$$$. Output the integer equal to $$$p \cdot q^{-1} \bmod M$$$. In other words, output such an integer $$$x$$$ that $$$0 \le x < M$$$ and $$$x \cdot q \equiv p \pmod{M}$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first example, the expected total length is $$$\int_0^1 \int_0^1 |x-y| \,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y = {1\over 3}$$$, and $$$3^{-1}$$$ modulo $$$998244353$$$ is $$$332748118$$$.

import sys

MD = 998244353

def init(n):
    ch = [[0] * (1 + n) for _ in range(1 + n)]
    ch[0][0] = 1
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        ch[i][0] = 1
        for j in range(1, i + 1):
            ch[i][j] = (ch[i - 1][j] + ch[i - 1][j - 1]) % MD
    return ch

def power(a, k):
    if k == 0:
        return 1
    p = power(a, k // 2)
    p = (p * p) % MD
    if k % 2 == 1:
        p = (p * a) % MD
    return p

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    k = int(data[1])
    l = int(data[2])
    
    ch = init(n)
    
    pp = [0] * (1 + n + n)

import sys

def multiply(a, b, n):
    ab = a * b
    return ab % n

def inverse(a, n):
    m = n
    r1, r2 = 1, 0
    r3, r4 = 0, 1
    while a > 0 and n > 0:
        if n >= a:
            r3 -= r1 * (n // a)
            r4 -= r2 * (n // a)
            n = n % a
        else:
            a, n = n, a
            r1, r3 = r3, r1
            r2, r4 = r4, r2
    if a == 0:
        return r3 % m if r3 >= 0 else (m + r3 % m)
    else:
        return r1 % m if r1 >= 0 else (m + r1 % m)

def main():
    P = 998244353
    
    input_line = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    parts = input_line.split()
    n = int(parts[0])
    real_k = int(parts[1])
    l = int(parts[2])
    
    # generate factorials
    factorials = [0] * (2 * n + 2)
    factorials[0] = 1
    for i in range(1, 2 * n + 2):
        factorials[i] = multiply(factorials[i-1], i, P)
    
    # number of ways to choose k pairs from 2k elements
    # where order doesn't matter
    # equals (2k)!/(2^k)/k! = (2k-1)!!
    doublefact = [0] * (n + 1)
    doublefact[0] = 1
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        doublefact[i] = multiply(doublefact[i-1], 2*i - 1, P)
    
    # list[r][k] stores for rth segment, exactly k of the n segments covering it
    list_table = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(2 * n + 2)]
    
    for r in range(1, 2 * n + 2):
        for k in range(1, n + 1):
            if ((r % 2) != (k % 2)) and (r - 1 >= k) and (2 * n + 1 - r >= k):
                num = multiply(factorials[r-1], factorials[2*n+1-r], P)
                num = multiply(num, doublefact[(r - k - 1) // 2], P)
                num = multiply(num, doublefact[(2 * n + 1 - r - k) // 2], P)
                
                denom = multiply(factorials[r - k - 1], factorials[2 * n + 1 - r - k], P)
                denom = multiply(denom, factorials[k], P)
                
                list_table[r][k] = multiply(num, inverse(multiply(denom, doublefact[n], P), P), P)
    
    ans = 0
    for r in range(1, 2 * n + 2):
        for k in range(real_k, n + 1):
            ans += list_table[r][k]
            ans %= P
    
    ans = multiply(ans, l, P)
    ans = multiply(ans, inverse(2 * n + 1, P), P)
    
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
import math

def enumFIF(n, mod):
    f = [1] * (n + 1)
    invf = [1] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        f[i] = f[i - 1] * i % mod
    # Compute modular inverse of f[n] using extended Euclidean algorithm
    a, b = f[n], mod
    p, q = 1, 0
    while b > 0:
        c = a // b
        a, b = b, a % b
        p, q = q, p - c * q
    invf[n] = p % mod
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        invf[i] = invf[i + 1] * (i + 1) % mod
    return [f, invf]

def C(n, r, mod, fif):
    if n < 0 or r < 0 or r > n:
        return 0
    return fif[0][n] * fif[1][r] % mod * fif[1][n - r] % mod

def pow_mod(a, n, mod):
    ret = 1
    a %= mod
    while n > 0:
        if n & 1:
            ret = ret * a % mod
        a = a * a % mod
        n >>= 1
    return ret

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data:
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    K = int(data[1])
    L = int(data[2])
    mod = 998244353
    fif = enumFIF(10000, mod)
    muls = [0] * (n + 1)
    
    for i in range(K, n + 1):
        m = C(n, i, mod, fif)
        for j in range(i, n + 1):
            sign = 1 if (j - i) % 2 == 0 else -1
            muls[j] = (muls[j] + m * C(n - i, n - j, mod, fif) * sign) % mod
    
    ans = 0
    for i in range(K, n + 1):
        term = pow_mod(2, i, mod) * fif[0][i] % mod
        term = term * fif[0][i] % mod
        term = term * fif[1][2 * i + 1] % mod
        term = term * muls[i] % mod
        ans = (ans + term) % mod
    
    if ans < 0:
        ans += mod
    result = ans * L % mod
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys

mod = 998244353

# Precompute binomial coefficients
max_n = int(2e3) + 2
cnk = [[0] * max_n for _ in range(max_n)]
cnk[0][0] = 1
for i in range(1, max_n):
    cnk[0][i] = 1
    for j in range(1, i + 1):
        cnk[j][i] = (cnk[j-1][i-1] + cnk[j][i-1]) % mod

# Precompute factorials
max_fact = 2 * max_n
fact = [1] * max_fact
for i in range(1, max_fact):
    fact[i] = (fact[i-1] * i) % mod

# Precompute powers of 2
deg_2 = [1] * max_n
for i in range(1, max_n):
    deg_2[i] = (deg_2[i-1] * 2) % mod

# Precompute modular inverses of odd factorials
reverse = [0] * max_fact
reverse[1] = 1
for i in range(3, max_fact, 2):
    reverse[i] = pow(fact[i], mod-2, mod)

def bin_pow(a, b, mod):
    ans = 1
    while b != 0:
        if b & 1:
            ans = (ans * a) % mod
        a = (a * a) % mod
        b >>= 1
    return ans

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()

import sys

MOD = 998244353
stirling = [[0] * 5001 for _ in range(5001)]
stirling[0][0] = 1

for i in range(1, 5001):
    for j in range(1, 5001):
        stirling[i][j] = (stirling[i-1][j-1] % MOD + (j * stirling[i-1][j]) % MOD) % MOD

def mod_inverse(x, p):
    return power(x, p-2, p)

def power(x, y, p):
    res = 1
    x = x % p
    while y > 0:
        if y % 2 == 1:
            res = (res * x) % p
        y = y >> 1
        x = (x * x) % p
    return res

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.readline().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    k = int(data[2])
    
    p = mod_inverse(m, MOD)
    val = 1
    ans = 0
    prob = 1
    
    for i in range(k, 0, -1):
        val = (val * (n - (k - i))) % MOD
        prob = (prob * p) % MOD
        ans = (ans + ((val * prob) % MOD * stirling[k][k - i + 1]) % MOD) % MOD
    
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: A string a of length m is called antipalindromic iff m is even, and for each i (1 ≤ i ≤ m) ai ≠ am - i + 1.Ivan has a string s consisting of n lowercase Latin letters; n is even. He wants to form some string t that will be an antipalindromic permutation of s. Also Ivan has denoted the beauty of index i as bi, and the beauty of t as the sum of bi among all indices i such that si = ti.Help Ivan to determine maximum possible beauty of t he can get.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line contains one integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100, n is even) — the number of characters in s. The second line contains the string s itself. It consists of only lowercase Latin letters, and it is guaranteed that its letters can be reordered to form an antipalindromic string. The third line contains n integer numbers b1, b2, ..., bn (1 ≤ bi ≤ 100), where bi is the beauty of index i.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one number — the maximum possible beauty of t.

    def link_(self, i, j, c, w):

        if i > self.cnt:

                i = j

        u = self.pq[1]
        v = self.pq[self.cnt]
        self.cnt -= 1
        if v != u:
            self.iq[v] = 1
            self.pq_dn(v)
        self.iq[u] = 0
        return u
    
    def dijkstra(self, s, t):
        self.dd = [self.INF] * self.n_
        self.dd[s] = 0
        self.kk = [0] * self.n_
        self.cnt = 0
        self.pq_add_last(s)
        
        while self.cnt > 0:

            h = h_ >> 1
            self.cc[h_] -= 1
            self.cc[h_ ^ 1] += 1
            t ^= self.ii[h] ^ self.jj[h]
        return 1
    
    def edmonds_karp(self, s, t):
        for h in range(self.m_):
            i = self.ii[h]
            j = self.jj[h]
            self.dd[j] = min(self.dd[j], self.dd[i] + self.ww[h])

            j = self.jj[h]
            self.ww_[h] = self.ww[h] + self.dd[i] - self.dd[j]

            for h in range(self.m_):

                j = self.jj[h]
                if self.dd[i] != self.INF and self.dd[j] != self.INF:

        cost = 0
        for h in range(self.m_):
            cost += self.ww[h] * self.cc[(h << 1) | 1]
        return cost

import sys
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
from functools import cmp_to_key

class Char:
    def __init__(self, chr, val, idx):
        self.chr = chr
        self.val = val
        self.idx = idx

def isAntiPalindrome(chars):
    n = len(chars)
    for i in range(n // 2):
        if chars[i] == chars[n - i - 1]:
            return False
    return True

def main():
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    if not input_data:
        return
    
    n = int(input_data[0].strip())
    s = input_data[1].strip()
    chars = list(s)
    
    vals = list(map(int, input_data[2].split()))
    
    wrongChars = []
    chars1 = []
    
    for i in range(n // 2):
        if vals[i] > vals[n - i - 1]:
            # swap chars and vals
            chars[i], chars[n - i - 1] = chars[n - i - 1], chars[i]
            vals[i], vals[n - i - 1] = vals[n - i - 1], vals[i]
        
        chr_obj = Char(chars[i], vals[i], i)
        if chars[i] == chars[n - i - 1]:
            wrongChars.append(chr_obj)
        chars1.append(chr_obj)
    
    # sort chars1 by val
    chars1.sort(key=lambda c: c.val)
    
    diff = 0
    
    if not isAntiPalindrome(chars):
        if len(wrongChars) == 1:
            wrongChar = wrongChars[0]
            for i in range(n // 2):
                chr_obj = chars1[i]
                if chr_obj.chr != wrongChar.chr and chars[n - chr_obj.idx - 1] != wrongChar.chr:
                    diff = wrongChar.val + chr_obj.val
                    break
        elif len(wrongChars) > 1:
            # Count occurrences of characters in wrongChars
            char_counts = Counter(c.chr for c in wrongChars)
            max_entry = max(char_counts.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])
            max_char = max_entry[0]
            
            append = []
            while max_entry[1] * 2 > len(wrongChars) + len(append):
                for i in range(n // 2):
                    chr_obj = chars1[i]
                    if (chr_obj.chr != max_char and 
                        chars[n - chr_obj.idx - 1] != max_char and 
                        chr_obj not in wrongChars and 
                        chr_obj not in append):
                        append.append(chr_obj)
                        char_counts[chr_obj.chr] += 1
                        if chr_obj.chr == max_char:
                            max_entry = (max_char, char_counts[max_char])
                        break
                else:
                    break
            
            diff = sum(c.val for c in wrongChars) + sum(c.val for c in append)
    
    total_sum = sum(vals)
    print(total_sum - diff)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            e.complement.flow -= minflow
            e = inedge[e.from_node]

        nonlocal ptr
        num = 0
        b = input_data[ptr]
        ptr += 1
        minus = False
        if b == '-':
            minus = True
            b = input_data[ptr]
            ptr += 1
        
        num = int(b)
        return -num if minus else num
    
    def ns(n):
        nonlocal ptr
        result = input_data[ptr]
        ptr += 1
        return result[:n]
    
    def na(n):
        nonlocal ptr
        a = [ni() for _ in range(n)]
        return a
    
    n = ni()
    s = list(ns(n))
    
    f = [0] * 26
    for c in s:
        f[ord(c) - ord('a')] += 1
    
    for i in range(26):
        if f[i] > n // 2:
            print(-1)
            return
    
    a = na(n)
    
    for i in range(n // 2):
        if a[i] > a[n - 1 - i]:
            a[i], a[n - 1 - i] = a[n - 1 - i], a[i]
            s[i], s[n - 1 - i] = s[n - 1 - i], s[i]
    
    es = []
    src = n
    sink = n + 1
    
    for i in range(n // 2):
        es.append(Edge(src, i, 1, 0))
        es.append(Edge(n - 1 - i, sink, 1, 0))
        for j in range(n // 2):

                cost = 0 if i == j else a[i]
                es.append(Edge(i, n - 1 - j, 1, cost))
    
    ans = sum(a)
    graph = compileWD(sink + 1, es)
    min_flow_cost = solveMinCostFlow(graph, src, sink, n)
    print(ans - min_flow_cost)

problem_description.description: Having problems with tram routes in the morning, Arkady decided to return home by metro. Fortunately for Arkady, there is only one metro line in the city.Unfortunately for Arkady, the line is circular. It means that the stations are enumerated from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ and there is a tunnel between any pair of consecutive stations as well as between the station $$$1$$$ and the station $$$n$$$. Trains that go in clockwise direction visit the stations in order $$$1 \to 2 \to 3 \to \ldots \to n \to 1$$$ while the trains that go in the counter-clockwise direction visit the stations in the reverse order.The stations that have numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ have interior mostly in red colors while the stations that have numbers from $$$m + 1$$$ to $$$n$$$ have blue interior. Arkady entered the metro at station $$$s$$$ and decided to use the following algorithm to choose his way home.  Initially he has a positive integer $$$t$$$ in his mind.  If the current station has red interior, he takes a clockwise-directed train, otherwise he takes a counter-clockwise-directed train.  He rides exactly $$$t$$$ stations on the train and leaves the train.  He decreases $$$t$$$ by one. If $$$t$$$ is still positive, he returns to step $$$2$$$. Otherwise he exits the metro. You have already realized that this algorithm most probably won't bring Arkady home. Find the station he will exit the metro at so that you can continue helping him.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le m < n$$$) — the total number of stations and the number of stations that have red interior. The second line contains two integers $$$s$$$ and $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le s \le n$$$, $$$1 \le t \le 10^{12}$$$) — the starting station and the initial value of $$$t$$$.
problem_description.output_spec: Output the only integer — the station where Arkady will exit the metro.
problem_description.notes: NoteConsider the first example. There are $$$10$$$ stations and the first $$$4$$$ of them are red. Arkady starts at station $$$3$$$ with value $$$t = 1$$$, so just rides $$$1$$$ station in clockwise direction and ends up on the station $$$4$$$.In the second example the metro is same as in the first example, but Arkady starts at station $$$3$$$ with value $$$t = 5$$$.   It is a red station so he rides $$$5$$$ stations in clockwise direction and leaves the train at station $$$8$$$.  It is a blue station, so he rides $$$4$$$ stations in counter-clockwise direction and leaves at station $$$4$$$.  It is a red station, so he rides $$$3$$$ stations in clockwise direction and leaves at station $$$7$$$.  It is a blue station, so he rides $$$2$$$ stations in counter-clockwise direction and leaves at station $$$5$$$.  It is a blue station, so he rides $$$1$$$ station in counter-clockwise direction and leaves at station $$$4$$$.  Now $$$t = 0$$$, so Arkady exits metro at the station $$$4$$$.

problem_description.description: zscoder has a deck of $$$n+m$$$ custom-made cards, which consists of $$$n$$$ cards labelled from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ jokers. Since zscoder is lonely, he wants to play a game with himself using those cards. Initially, the deck is shuffled uniformly randomly and placed on the table. zscoder has a set $$$S$$$ which is initially empty. Every second, zscoder draws the top card from the deck.   If the card has a number $$$x$$$ written on it, zscoder removes the card and adds $$$x$$$ to the set $$$S$$$.  If the card drawn is a joker, zscoder places all the cards back into the deck and reshuffles (uniformly randomly) the $$$n+m$$$ cards to form a new deck (hence the new deck now contains all cards from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ and the $$$m$$$ jokers). Then, if $$$S$$$ currently contains all the elements from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, the game ends. Shuffling the deck doesn't take time at all. What is the expected number of seconds before the game ends? We can show that the answer can be written in the form $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P, Q$$$ are relatively prime integers and $$$Q \neq 0 \bmod 998244353$$$. Output the value of $$$(P \cdot Q^{-1})$$$ modulo $$$998244353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line of the input contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 2 \cdot 10^{6}$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output a single integer, the value of $$$(P \cdot Q^{-1})$$$ modulo $$$998244353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteFor the first sample, it can be proven that the expected time before the game ends is $$$5$$$ seconds.For the second sample, it can be proven that the expected time before the game ends is $$$\frac{28}{3}$$$ seconds.

import sys
import math

def invl(a, mod):
    b = mod
    p, q = 1, 0
    while b > 0:
        c = a // b
        d = a
        a = b
        b = d % b
        d = p
        p = q
        q = d - c * q
    return p % mod

def solve():
    mod = 998244353
    n, m = map(int, input().split())
    
    inv_m1 = invl(m + 1, mod)
    ans = (1 + inv_m1 * n) % mod
    
    base = inv_m1 * ((m * (m + 2 + (n - 1))) % mod) % mod
    
    u = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        u += invl(i, mod)
        u %= mod
    
    ans = (base * u + ans) % mod
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()

problem_description.description: Sometimes Mister B has free evenings when he doesn't know what to do. Fortunately, Mister B found a new game, where the player can play against aliens.All characters in this game are lowercase English letters. There are two players: Mister B and his competitor.Initially the players have a string s consisting of the first a English letters in alphabetical order (for example, if a = 5, then s equals to "abcde").The players take turns appending letters to string s. Mister B moves first.Mister B must append exactly b letters on each his move. He can arbitrary choose these letters. His opponent adds exactly a letters on each move.Mister B quickly understood that his opponent was just a computer that used a simple algorithm. The computer on each turn considers the suffix of string s of length a and generates a string t of length a such that all letters in the string t are distinct and don't appear in the considered suffix. From multiple variants of t lexicographically minimal is chosen (if a = 4 and the suffix is "bfdd", the computer chooses string t equal to "aceg"). After that the chosen string t is appended to the end of s.Mister B soon found the game boring and came up with the following question: what can be the minimum possible number of different letters in string s on the segment between positions l and r, inclusive. Letters of string s are numerated starting from 1.
problem_description.input_spec: First and only line contains four space-separated integers: a, b, l and r (1 ≤ a, b ≤ 12, 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 109) — the numbers of letters each player appends and the bounds of the segment.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer — the minimum possible number of different letters in the segment from position l to position r, inclusive, in string s.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample test one of optimal strategies generate string s = "abababab...", that's why answer is 2.In the second sample test string s = "abcdbcaefg..." can be obtained, chosen segment will look like "bcdbc", that's why answer is 3.In the third sample test string s = "abczzzacad..." can be obtained, chosen, segment will look like "zzz", that's why answer is 1.

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    a = int(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    b = int(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    l = int(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    l -= 1
    r = int(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    total = a + b
    r -= l // total * total
    l -= l // total * total
    
    if r > total * 3:
        r -= r // total * total
        r += total * 3
    
    seq = list(range(r))
    
    # First pass
    i = a
    while i < r:
        if i % total < a:
            used = set()
            for j in range(i - 1, max(-1, i - a - 1), -1):
                used.add(seq[j])
            
            while i % total != a and i < r:
                j = 0
                while j in used:
                    j += 1
                used.add(j)
                seq[i] = j
                i += 1
        else:
            seq[i] = seq[i - 1]
            i += 1
    
    # Calculate result for first segment
    used = set()
    for i in range(l, r):
        used.add(seq[i])
    result = len(used)
    
    # Modify sequence
    for i in range(a, min(a + b, r)):
        if b < r:
            seq[i] = seq[b]
    
    # Second pass
    i = a + b
    while i < r:
        if i % total < a:
            used = set()
            for j in range(i - 1, max(-1, i - a - 1), -1):
                used.add(seq[j])
            
            while i % total != a and i < r:
                j = 0
                while j in used:
                    j += 1
                used.add(j)
                seq[i] = j
                i += 1
        else:
            seq[i] = seq[i - 1]
            i += 1
    
    # Calculate result for second segment
    used = set()
    for i in range(l, r):
        used.add(seq[i])
    result = min(result, len(used))
    
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
